knowledge_tree.title: PEP English Grade 6 Book 2
knowledge_tree.content: English textbook for Grade 6, second semester (PEP edition), covering key language points including comparative adjectives, past tense, holiday activities, and describing changes.

children.title: Unit 1 How tall are you?
children.content: Unit focusing on comparative adjectives to describe people and things.

children.title: Comparative Adjectives
children.content: Adjectives used to compare two or more things, often formed by adding -er or using 'more'.

children.title: Formation of Comparative Adjectives
children.content: For short adjectives, add -er (e.g., tall → taller). For adjectives ending in -y, change -y to -i and add -er (e.g., happy → happier). For longer adjectives, use 'more' (e.g., more beautiful).

children.title: Irregular Comparative Forms
children.content: Some adjectives have irregular comparative forms (e.g., good → better, bad → worse, far → farther/further).

children.title: Asking about Height and Weight
children.content: Questions and responses about physical attributes like height and weight.

children.title: How tall are you?
children.content: Question to ask about someone's height. Response: 'I am [height] metres/tall.'

children.title: How heavy are you?
children.content: Question to ask about someone's weight. Response: 'I am [weight] kilograms.'

children.title: Using 'than' in Comparisons
children.content: The word 'than' is used to link two parts of a comparison.

children.title: Structure with 'than'
children.content: Subject + verb + comparative adjective + than + object (e.g., I am taller than you).

children.title: Unit 2 Last weekend
children.content: Unit focusing on past simple tense to talk about completed actions in the past.

children.title: Past Simple Tense
children.content: Tense used to describe actions that happened and were completed in the past.

children.title: Regular Past Tense Verbs
children.content: For most verbs, add -ed to form the past tense (e.g., play → played). For verbs ending in -e, add -d (e.g., like → liked). For verbs ending in a consonant + -y, change -y to -i and add -ed (e.g., study → studied).

children.title: Irregular Past Tense Verbs
children.content: Some verbs have irregular past tense forms (e.g., go → went, see → saw, have → had).

children.title: Talking about Past Activities
children.content: Questions and responses about what someone did in the past.

children.title: What did you do last weekend?
children.content: Question to ask about past activities. Response: 'I [past tense verb]...' (e.g., I watched TV).

children.title: Time Expressions for Past
children.content: Words and phrases like 'last weekend', 'yesterday', 'last night' used with past tense.

children.title: Unit 3 Where did you go?
children.content: Unit focusing on past tense questions and talking about holidays and trips.

children.title: Past Tense Questions
children.content: Forming questions about past events using 'did'.

children.title: Did you...? Questions
children.content: Yes/No questions about the past: Did + subject + base verb? (e.g., Did you go to Turpan?).

children.title: Wh- Questions in Past Tense
children.content: Questions starting with what, where, when, how, etc., followed by did + subject + base verb (e.g., Where did you go?).

children.title: Talking about Holidays
children.content: Vocabulary and phrases related to holiday activities.

children.title: Holiday Activities Vocabulary
children.content: Words like went camping, went fishing, rode a horse, took pictures, bought gifts, ate fresh food.

children.title: Describing Holiday Experiences
children.content: Using past tense to describe what you did and saw on holiday (e.g., It was warm. I went swimming).

children.title: Unit 4 Then and now
children.content: Unit focusing on describing changes over time using past and present tenses.

children.title: Describing Changes
children.content: Using 'before' and 'now' to talk about how things or people were different in the past.

children.title: There was/were...
children.content: Using 'there was' (singular) and 'there were' (plural) to describe things that existed in the past but not now.

children.title: There is/are...
children.content: Using 'there is' (singular) and 'there are' (plural) to describe things that exist now.

children.title: Talking about Personal Changes
children.content: Describing how oneself or others have changed over time.

children.title: I was... I am...
children.content: Structure to describe personal changes (e.g., Before, I was quiet. Now, I am active).

children.title: I couldn't... I can...
children.content: Structure to describe abilities that have changed (e.g., I was short, so I couldn't ride well. Now I go cycling every day).

children.title: Recycle: Mike's happy days
children.content: Review unit consolidating vocabulary and grammar from previous units.

children.title: Word Groups and Categories
children.content: Grouping words into categories like fruit, clothes, animals, etc.

children.title: Describing People and Activities
children.content: Using present simple and present continuous tenses to describe current actions and states.

children.title: Sequencing Past Events
children.content: Using words like first, then, next, after that, finally to describe a sequence of past actions.

triplets.head: Talking about Past Activities
triplets.tail: What did you do last weekend?
